summary: In this excerpt from a fiction book, the narrator and companions search an overgrown, decrepit shack by a waterway for a man named Wheeze, who answers from the dark claiming to have a knife. They find him sick, feverish, and injured, then help him to their car. Bree examines his badly swollen ankle, gives him leftover Vicodin and a sports drink, and wraps the ankle in elastic bandage.
one_line: Narrator and friends find a feverish, injured Wheeze hiding in a derelict shack and tend to his ankle.
key_facts: The narrator searches a dilapidated shack surrounded by overgrowth for a guy named Wheeze.
A hoarse voice from the gloom says, "I have a knife," before the narrator finds Wheeze.
Wheeze had told the narrator stories about creepy guys he ran into while riding the rails.
A towboat made a low, mournful hoot out over the water near the shack.
Wheeze is shaking with cold, his skin feels hot to the touch, and his eyes look like he cannot quite focus.
Wheeze had surrounded himself with cardboard and dead leaves to try to keep warm.
Nikko and the narrator help Wheeze hop and get dragged out of the shed and through the trees to the car.
Bree examines Wheeze's ankle as he lowers himself onto the backseat of the car.
Wheeze's ankle is badly swollen, and Bree says it looks like it belongs to an elephant.
Bree gives Wheeze Vicodin left over from when she had her wisdom teeth taken out.
Bree opens a bottle of a neon-colored sports drink so Wheeze can swallow the pills.
Bree cuts off Wheeze's grotty sock and wraps the ankle with stretchy elastic bandage.
Bree's roommate plays Lacrosse, and the group has a ton of elastic bandages.
Wheeze clamps his teeth on his lower lip as his face goes white and sweaty while the wrapping is secured with metal clips.
